name: gimp-agent-mcp
tagline: The whole of GIMP 3 for AI agents: everyday edits, one undo step, pixel checks, and recipes. Tested on Windows, Linux and macOS.
summary: An MCP server that hands AI agents the whole of GIMP 3 rather than a hand-picked slice. Every one of GIMP's roughly 1,000 Procedure Database functions and 207 GEGL filters is reachable through runtime introspection, so nothing goes stale when GIMP updates. The agent can see its work: a PNG render after each step, before/after/diff comparisons, and pixel measurement instead of guessing. Recipes turn repeatable jobs (stickers, icon sets, watermarks, contact sheets, social cards from a layout manifest) into one call, and a batch runner applies them to whole folders. Version 0.5.0 groups a batch of edits into one undo step and is exercised against real GIMP on Windows, Linux and macOS.
highlights: Tools, reusable recipes and bundled skills for layered assets, sprite sheets and batch jobs
Runtime introspection of the PDB and GEGL, with typed argument descriptions and enum choices read from GIMP at call time
Render, measure, snapshot and compare so the agent verifies each edit before moving on
Non-destructive layer effects, selections, masks, text, vector paths and AI subject cut-outs
Works inside the GIMP window you already have open: Filters, Development, Start Agent Bridge
One Ctrl+Z reverts a whole gimp_edit_batch turn, proven on live GIMP for Windows, Linux and macOS.
install: claude mcp add gimp -- uvx gimp-agent-mcp serve

review.summary: Package and release documentation checked at 0.5.0. Cross-platform GIMP checks are recorded upstream; this review did not repeat visible-window or fresh-install tests.

name: jobscout-mcp
tagline: Privacy-first job discovery across sources: normalisation, deduplication and provenance for every listing.
summary: A multi-source job discovery engine exposed as MCP tools. It searches several boards, normalises each listing into one record, deduplicates across sources on a shared key space, and keeps provenance so an agent can say where a role came from. It deliberately stops at discovery: the judgement about whether a role fits belongs to the person, or to a private layer that never leaves their machine.
highlights: Several providers behind one normalised record
Deterministic deduplication with provenance on every listing
AI and Web3 taxonomy for the lanes the author actually works in
Listed in the official MCP Registry and published on npm

review.summary: Published package remains 0.2.1. Main includes unreleased We Work Remotely and RemoteOK adapters. Provider reliability and installation evidence are still needed before a stable release.

name: website-content-mcp
tagline: A site-scoped content gateway: the pages, structure and text of a website in a form agents can reason over.
summary: Exposes a website's content to agents as structured, read-only tools: page inventory, headings, body text and metadata, scoped to sites the operator owns. It is the open-source foundation for managed web intelligence work, and runs live as read-only endpoints for the author's own sites.
highlights: Read-only by design, scoped per site
Structured page, heading and metadata output rather than raw HTML
Published on npm; runs as hosted endpoints for owned sites
install: claude mcp add website-content --env SITE_BASE_URL=https://example.com -- npx -y --package @sarutobi-sasuke/website-content-mcp website-content-stdio
limitations: Replace https://example.com in the install command with the public site you want to expose. Other clients must also set SITE_BASE_URL in the server environment.

review.summary: Published package remains 0.3.1. The proposed 0.4.0 hardening is in a separate pull request and is not included in the published package.

name: agent-handoff-mcp
tagline: Local-first, bounded, auditable handoffs between AI agents. A coordination primitive, not a message bus.
summary: A vendor-neutral way for one agent to hand work to another with a record of what was handed over, to whom, and what happened next. Handoffs are bounded messages with lifecycle state; a handoff can reference a repository or vault artefact without gaining any authority to read or change it.
highlights: Lifecycle state and receipts for every handoff
Works across Claude, Codex and any stdio MCP client
Content-free evidence path: identities and artefacts are referenced, never copied

review.summary: The source changelog records policy, revocation and packaged-transport fixes. A first tagged package and operational proof are still required for promotion.

name: credential-broker-mcp
tagline: Agents use gated APIs through scoped, audited requests without ever seeing the secret.
summary: A policy-gated broker that lets an agent exercise a credential without holding it. The agent asks for an operation; the broker checks scope and policy, performs the call, logs it, and returns the result. Secrets stay on the operator's side.
highlights: Scoped grants per agent and per operation
Every request audited
Local-first; no secret ever enters an agent's context

review.summary: The source records policy v2 and secret-handling fixes plus a Windows key manager. This metadata review does not establish security readiness or a published release.

name: obsidian-github-mcp
tagline: Permissioned proposal gateway for Obsidian vaults stored on GitHub: agents propose, humans merge.
summary: Agents propose bounded changes on isolated GitHub branches within the paths and rules the operator allows. A human reviews and merges through the repository workflow. The gateway can be configured for different Obsidian vaults kept in GitHub.
highlights: Proposal branches keep suggested changes separate from the protected vault branch
Path and rule permissions per agent
Works with any Obsidian vault kept in a GitHub repository

review.summary: Release preparation is on main, with no first tag recorded at review. A disposable proposal workflow and denied-write evidence remain promotion requirements.

name: source-pack-mcp
tagline: Structured research source packs: facts, quotes, numbers, primary links and a coverage map, with provenance.
summary: Turns fetched public pages into a source pack: candidate facts, quotations, numbers and links, with a coverage map and extraction limits. A recorded source and retrieval date show where evidence came from; they do not establish that a claim is true.
highlights: Extracted facts, quotes and numbers retain their source links
Coverage map shows the gaps as well as the finds
Fetcher hardened against server-side request forgery

review.summary: The README distinguishes fetched candidate evidence from verified truth. Source installation and SSRF checks are documented; a versioned package and extraction benchmark are still needed.

name: meeting-context-router
tagline: Proposal-first routing from meeting tools into governed CRM and knowledge-system updates.
summary: Takes the output of meeting tools (transcripts, summaries, action items) and routes it as proposals into the CRM and knowledge systems that should hold it, rather than writing directly. A bounded stdio MCP surface sits on top so agents can ask what a meeting changed.
highlights: Proposal-first: nothing is written to a system of record without review
Bounded tool surface for agents
Designed around Fireflies-style meeting exports

review.summary: The roadmap records a proposal queue, delivery retries and retention controls. A real reviewed meeting-to-destination workflow remains unproven in this review.

name: mcp-dashboard
tagline: Cost and benefit dashboard for your MCP toolbox across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor.
summary: A local dashboard that reads the MCP configuration of the agent clients on your machine and shows what each server costs you in RAM and context tokens against how much you actually use it, with working on/off switches. Not an MCP server itself: a control surface for the fleet.
highlights: Reads Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor configurations
RAM, context tokens and real usage per server
On/off switches that write back safely

review.summary: Version 1.0.0 is published. The roadmap still contains release-candidate wording and incomplete real-machine and usage gates, so the preview label is retained.

name: sports-oracle-teneo-agent
tagline: Teneo agent wrapping the Sports Oracle API: live NBA, NHL, MLB, NFL, F1, soccer, tennis and MMA data for agents.
summary: An experimental agent that exposes live sports data through both a REST interface and an MCP transport, built to explore how a data provider looks from inside an agent network.
highlights: REST and MCP transports on the same data
Eight sports covered
Experimental; requires a separately configured provider API credential

name: Unofficial Telegram Personal Proxy
tagline: A local MCP tool for Telegram folders, reviewed outreach and follow-up tracking. Private preview in active development.
summary: I built this for work spread across Telegram groups and folders. An agent can find the right chats, prepare outreach for review, record send results and surface follow-up candidates. It runs locally and is in daily personal use. The next step is to make the attention queue more accurate and the package easier for someone else to set up.
highlights: Folder discovery, scoped conversation reads and message search
Exact recipient and message previews, human approval before sending, and durable delivery receipts
Outreach campaigns with reviewed batches, group contacts and reply checks
Follow-up candidates with collection coverage and freshness limits
Local dashboard and browser approvals alongside the MCP workflow
availability: Private preview. There is no public download, hosted service, paid plan or ChatGPT store listing yet. The source is not public. Customer onboarding and commercial access requirements are still being assessed.
limitations: Group activity after a message is a follow-up signal, not proof that someone answered it. Reply-thread detection needs further work.
Collection is scoped and can be incomplete or stale. This is not a complete, continuous account monitor.
The current setup uses a personal Telegram cloud-chat session. Secret Chats are excluded.
Local session custody does not mean local AI processing: content returned to an AI client reaches that client.
A customer-ready install and ChatGPT connection are still being developed. Commercial AI use needs a resolved data-use and consent model.

name: Aseprite Agent MCP
tagline: Local pixel-art authoring, animation checks and verified Phaser exports from editable Aseprite masters. Private alpha.
summary: A local MCP server for creating and editing pixel art through Aseprite's CLI and Lua API. It keeps native masters, returns rendered previews, checks asset contracts and compares exported pixels with the reopened source. Built on an attributed MIT headless engine, it complements GIMP for sprite and animation work.
highlights: Native documents, drawing, layers, cels, palettes, frames, tags and slices
Typed batch edits with preview feedback and contract checks for geometry, tags, palette and alpha
Phaser sheets, atlas metadata and frame timing checked against reopened native masters
availability: Private alpha. There is no public source repository, package download or hosted endpoint yet.
limitations: Requires a separately installed Aseprite runtime with Lua support. No editor binary is included.
Synthetic pipeline checks do not establish artistic quality. An artist-reviewed directional cycle and real game asset workflow remain open gates.
Broader inherited-tool resource limits and dedicated resampling and fringe checks need further work.
The optional live-editor bridge is not implemented. Public release remains subject to source privacy and runtime distribution review.

name: astraeus-postgres-mcp
tagline: Governed, read-only Postgres access for agents: table and column allowlists, row caps, PII masking and an audit log.
summary: A local-first MCP server that lets an agent query Postgres through a policy layer instead of a raw connection string. It refuses to start without a policy file and a connection string. Each query must be one read-only, single-table SELECT: it is parsed with a real PostgreSQL parser, checked against the policy and regenerated from the validated syntax tree, so the text the agent sends is never executed as written. Every query runs in a read-only transaction with a statement timeout.
highlights: Five tools: list_tables, describe_table, query, policy_info and ping
Table and column allowlists, a row cap, an optional per-table predicate and PII masking, all from one policy file
Queries are rebuilt from the validated syntax tree; unknown syntax is denied, not guessed at
Append-only JSONL audit log of every allow and deny, with literals normalised and connection strings never logged
limitations: Version 0.1.0 on main. Not published to npm and not tagged; install from source.
v0 rejects joins, subqueries, CTEs and UNION, and runs over stdio only.
Joins, named views, Streamable HTTP and audit rotation are in an open v1 pull request and are not on main yet.
The guard is a filter, not a sandbox. The database role and row-level security remain the real boundary.

name: mcp-host-gateway
tagline: A hosted MCP edge: bearer auth, per-plan tool grants and rate limits in front of Streamable HTTP MCP servers.
summary: A small gateway that sits in front of product MCP servers so they can be offered hosted. A client connects over Streamable HTTP with a bearer token; the gateway verifies it, maps the caller to a plan, checks that the plan covers the upstream and the tool, applies a per-identity rate limit and forwards the JSON-RPC call. It carries no product logic of its own, and it fails closed at startup when its auth or upstream configuration is incomplete.
highlights: Bearer JWT verification against the issuer's JWKS, or static tokens for development
Plan-based grants per upstream and per tool, with tools/list filtered to what the caller may use
Per-identity token-bucket rate limits with clear 401, 403 and 429 JSON-RPC errors
JSON-line logs with tokens and secret-shaped keys redacted; request bodies are never logged
limitations: Version 0.1.0 on main. Deploy-only: not published to npm, not tagged, and not running as a public service yet.
v0 keeps rate-limit state in one process and buffers SSE responses instead of streaming them.
A shared rate store, streaming relay, Docker image and audit log are in open pull requests and are not on main yet.

name: mcp-eval-harness
tagline: Contract tests for MCP servers: expected tools, schema checks and golden fixtures, with CLI exit codes that can gate a release.
summary: A shared test harness for MCP servers. The mcp-eval CLI loads a YAML or JSON suite, starts the target server, runs each contract through the official MCP client, compares results with golden fixtures and JSON Schemas, and exits non-zero on any failure. It answers one question: does this server still honour the contract it published? It is not a hosted service and not an LLM judge.
highlights: Checks that expected tools exist and that advertised input schemas match a golden
Golden comparisons with only_paths and ignore_paths for timestamps and request ids
Error-path assertions for tool errors and JSON-RPC error codes
Golden files change only with an explicit --update-goldens flag, never implicitly
limitations: Version 0.1.0 on main. Not published to npm and not tagged; install from git.
v0 covers tool contracts only, and its own tests exercise stdio targets only.
Prompts and resources contracts, a composite Action and Streamable HTTP tests are in open pull requests and are not on main yet.
